nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Normative models trained using Bayesian linear regression (PCNtoolkit).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: normative models 58,61,62 were trained across all individuals using Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) 63 using PCNtoolkit package (version 0.26)

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Four imaging modalities were used: (1) Structural MRI: voxel-based morphometry (VBM)-derived voxel-wise gray matter (GM) volumes; (2) Resting-state fMRI: seed-based correlation between the FFA and remaining FFG voxels (FFA connectivity); (3) Task-fMRI: T-contrast maps reflecting sensitivity to faces (faces vs. shapes condition from Hariri paradigm); (4) EEG: principal component of source-reconstructed activation across cortical FFG parcels.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: the features for subsequent normative modeling were as follows (1) structure: voxel-based morphometry (VBM)-derived, voxel-wise GM volumes, (2) rs-fMRI: seed-based correlation between the FFA and the remaining FFG, (3) task-fMRI: T-contrast maps reflecting sensitivity to faces and (4) EEG: the principal component of source-reconstructed activation obtained across different cortical FFG parcels.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age (modeled with B-spline basis in primary analysis), sex, scanning site.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: modelling the relationship between each brain imaging modality (within the right and left FFG ROI) and age, sex and scanning site. In primary analysis, a B-spline basis expansion of the of covariate vector was used to model non-linear effects of age.
